job.title: Assistant Accountant
job.description:
About the Company
Quinn Allan is partnering with a highly regarded Australian legal firm with a strong reputation for excellence, collaboration and professional development. Known for its people-first culture and commitment to continuous improvement, the firm offers a supportive environment where employees are encouraged to develop their careers and make a meaningful impact.
With ongoing investment in its people, systems and processes, this is an excellent opportunity to join a stable and well-respected organisation offering broad exposure, strong mentorship and genuine career progression opportunities.
  
About the Position
Reporting to the Financial Accountant, the Assistant Accountant will play an important role within the Finance team, supporting the delivery of accurate financial reporting, month-end processes, reconciliations and compliance activities.
This is a broad and varied role that will provide exposure across financial accounting, reporting, treasury, accounts administration and continuous improvement initiatives. Working closely with stakeholders across the firm, you will help ensure the integrity of financial information while supporting key business processes and maintaining a high level of service to internal stakeholders.
The position is ideally suited to an ambitious accounting professional looking to further develop their technical accounting capabilities within a professional services environment, while receiving mentorship, support and structured development opportunities.
  
Duties
• Support month-end and year-end processes, including journals, accruals, prepayments and reconciliations
• Assist with management reporting, budgeting, forecasting and financial reporting activities
• Maintain general ledger integrity and support fixed asset accounting processes
• Prepare balance sheet, bank, trust and intercompany reconciliations, identifying and resolving variances as required
• Assist with regulatory and compliance obligations, including BAS preparation and reporting requirements
• Support treasury, banking administration and cash management activities
• Assist across accounts payable, billing and revenue processes as required
• Respond to finance-related queries and provide support to stakeholders across the firm
• Contribute to system enhancements, process improvement initiatives and finance automation projects
• Support audit requirements and broader finance team initiatives
  
About You
To be successful in this role, you will be a motivated and detail-oriented accounting professional who enjoys working collaboratively and is eager to further develop your technical accounting skills. You will take pride in producing accurate work, building strong stakeholder relationships and identifying opportunities to improve processes and efficiencies.
You will have:
• Degree qualifications in Accounting, Finance or Commerce
• CPA or CA studies underway, or the intention to commence in the near future
• 1-3 years' experience in an Assistant Accountant, Accounts Officer or similar finance role
• A sound understanding of accounting principles, financial reporting and reconciliations
• Experience preparing journals and working with general ledger accounts
• Strong Excel skills and confidence working with financial systems
• Excellent attention to detail, organisational and time management capabilities
• Strong communication skills and the ability to engage confidently with senior professional stakeholders
• A proactive mindset with a genuine interest in continuous improvement and process optimisation
Experience within a law firm, professional services or consulting environment will be highly regarded, as will exposure to ERP or practice management systems and involvement in audits, budgeting or management reporting activities.
  
How to Apply
Please click 'Apply' to submit your resume online, or contact Olivia Reiber on 0404 520 078 for a confidential discussion.

job.title: IT Support Technician
job.description:
We’re looking for a Level 1/2 IT Support Technician to join the technology team within the sports and entertainment industry.

You will act as the first point of contact for support requests logged through the service desk platform, providing triage, diagnosis and resolution of Level 1/2 issues for end users across the site.

You’ll log, categorise and resolve incidents within agreed SLAs, escalate to Level 2/3 support with clear documentation where needed, and help maintain a high standard of customer service for staff and stakeholders with varying levels of technical ability.
 
Key Responsibilities
  • Act as the first point of contact for support requests logged through the service desk platform.
  • Log, categorise and prioritise incidents and service requests accurately, resolving straightforward issues within Level 1/2 scope and agreed SLAs.
  • Perform initial triage and diagnosis of common issues, including password resets, account unlocks, printer and hardware faults, software installations and connectivity problems.
  • Provide account and permissions administration in Active Directory and Microsoft 365, including group membership, mailbox permissions and shared drive access.
  • Perform deeper diagnostics for recurring or non-standard issues such as software conflicts, application errors and basic network connectivity problems.
  • Support the imaging, configuration and deployment of desktops, laptops and mobile devices.
  • Escalate issues to Level 2/3 support with clear documentation of troubleshooting steps taken.
Process and Documentation
  • Follow documented standard operating procedures and escalation paths.
  • Maintain accurate and up-to-date records for every ticket worked.
  • Follow change management processes when applying standard fixes.
  • Contribute to and utilise the internal knowledge base, identifying recurring issues and supporting permanent fixes or improved documentation.
About You
  • Experience in an end-user IT support role, with exposure to Level 1/2 tasks such as account administration and device deployment.
  • Excellent understanding of Windows and Microsoft 365 environments, including Office Suite, Outlook, OneDrive, Teams, SharePoint, Azure and Intune.
  • Demonstrated experience with ITSM platforms such as Jira, Freshservice or ServiceNow.
  • Solid working knowledge of Active Directory and Microsoft 365 administration.
  • Understanding of core network fundamentals, including DHCP, DNS and VPN.
  • Experience with account and password management, including MFA.
  • Diploma or degree in Information Technology or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
  • CompTIA A+, MS-900, AZ-900 or ITIL 4 Foundation certification highly regarded but not essential.
Personal Attributes
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with a friendly and professional manner.
  • Strong attention to detail.
  • Ability to prioritise and manage multiple tasks simultaneously.
  • Willingness to learn new systems and processes quickly.
  • Team-oriented and collaborative approach.
  • Genuine customer-focused mindset.
Next Steps
Please click ‘Apply’ to submit your resume online or email Josh Tinton at jtinton@quinnallan.com.au.

job.title: Financial Accountant

job.title: Manager, Data Governance and Partnerships
job.description:
Manager, Data Governance & Partnerships

 Role: Manager, Data Governance & Partnerships
Reporting to: Head of Business Intelligence & Analytics
Location: Hawthorn, Melbourne
Division: Strategy & Service Design
Team: Individual contributor / cross-functional leadership
  
The Company
Eastern Melbourne Primary Health Network (EMPHN) is seeking a Manager, Data Governance & Partnerships to establish and lead its data governance function at a genuinely exciting point in the organisation’s evolution.

EMPHN is transforming how it commissions health services while developing a sophisticated linked healthcare data environment covering approximately 1.8 million people. With data governance currently operating across the organisation in a piecemeal way, this newly created role will bring the function together and establish the standards, processes and partnerships that will underpin EMPHN’s future data capability.

The Opportunity
Reporting to the Head of Business Intelligence & Analytics, you will sit within the Strategy & Service Design division and work across the organisation to establish practical, effective data governance.

This is a hands-on governance role. You will be expected to get into the detail of data schemas, collection processes, data sharing arrangements, controls and operational workflows, while simultaneously developing the broader governance framework.

You won't be managing a large team. In fact, there are no direct reports but scope to grow a team in the future.

Instead, your influence will come through your ability to work across clinicians, commissioners, program teams, executives, technology and external partners to make governance work in practice.
  
  
What You’ll be Responsible For
  • Build the governance function, Establish EMPHN's enterprise data governance framework, standards, policies, processes and controls from the ground up.
  • Own data sharing & partnerships, Own EMPHN's Data Sharing Agreement portfolio and establish effective governance across general practices, Outcome Health, research and data linkage partners.
  • Lead privacy, compliance & risk, Lead privacy, regulatory, information security, audit and data lifecycle requirements across EMPHN's data environment.
  • Own departmental data reporting, Lead mandatory Department of Health, Disability and Ageing reporting, including PIP QI, UP-MDS and GP-MDS, ensuring data is accurate, compliant and delivered on time.
What We’re Looking For
You'll likely come from a background in data governance, data management, information governance, privacy, data stewardship or a closely related discipline, with demonstrated experience establishing governance frameworks in complex environments.

More importantly, you'll be comfortable operating where the answer isn't already written.

You'll need to be able to:
  • Build a governance function from the ground up.
  • Translate regulatory, contractual and privacy obligations into practical processes.
  • Work comfortably with technical data concepts and schemas.
  • Navigate complex stakeholder environments without relying on formal authority.
  • Build relationships across clinical, operational, technology and executive teams.
  • Balance strategic thinking with hands-on delivery.
  • Bring structure to an evolving and immature governance environment.
Your value will come from translating legal, contractual and regulatory requirements into governance that people can actually use.

The EMPHN employee proposition
Alongside genuine population-level impact, EMPHN offers:
  • 13 weeks paid parental leave after six months' service.
  • Two work-life balance days each year.
  • Three additional paid days over Christmas.
  • Purchased leave.
  • Not-for-profit salary packaging benefits.
  • Paid study leave.
  • First Peoples Cultural Leave.
  • Gender Affirmation Leave.
Interested?
If you're a data governance professional who enjoys building rather than maintaining, and you want the opportunity to shape a function that will underpin a significant population-health data strategy, we'd like to hear from you.

Hit the “Apply” button below or reach out to Ty Erasmus at terasmus@quinnallan.com.au or 0461 410 477.
